_comment: Spec 220: how a project's code-landing choice resolves, as one table both
implementations are checked against. `aide-run-spec` (bash) and the dashboard's
resolveCodeLanding() (TypeScript) read it independently — the pair is hand-kept,
like WORKFLOW_STEPS, DEPENDENCY_GATED_STEPS and the worktree links, so the
agreement is asserted rather than assumed.
Unlike the worktree links this has NO .aide/config fallback: the choice is a team
policy about review, not a per-machine preference, and a gitignored file silently
overriding the committed manifest is exactly the drift the manifest was picked to
avoid. The `config` column is there to prove the old-style spelling is IGNORED.
`landing` is what both sides must resolve to. `push` is the mode aide-run-spec must
run with when no --push was typed on the command line; the dashboard's own column
is the same answer, since a `pr` landing forces `--push pr` over the global default.
null means: the key is not written in that file at all.
